messages:
kevin: Heads up — saw slow, steady GPU memory climb on dedicated pool during long batched chat runs. ~700MB growth / 24h on a single worker. Repro attached below.

lisa: :eyes: which model / config?

kevin: gptj-6b-quant, seq=512, batch=16, streaming=true, kv cache on. Only shows up when we keep feeding new prompts for hours (not single-shot stress).

kevin: Quick repro (runs on any canary node):
```bash
# run in rwd/infer:canary container
python tests/repro/batched_growth.py --model gptj-6b-quant --bs 16 --seq 512 --duration 2h --stream
```

dmitri: Can you paste the pynvml/resident/reserved numbers? Also have we ruled out host-side OOM/swap dance?

kevin: Pynvml snapshot from ~2h in: resident=3.2GB, reserved=5.6GB, nvml_util=12%. Native allocator arenas show repeated +256MB churn in reserved but resident only slowly climbs.

maria: That smells like workspace / arena rounding causing growth (workspaces resizing to accommodate a rare long sequence). Do we have a histogram of max_seq per request?

kevin: Yes — seq distribution in the run has tail at 512 but 95% at 128. We think a few rare 512s trigger persistent workspace increases.

aj: Could be fragmentation vs leak. If allocator is keeping large slabs due to sizing policy, reserved grows but not necessarily leaked. Any slab lifetime info?

kevin: I captured allocator debug log (attached) — arenas 0/1 show repeated alloc of size ~34M followed by free but arena doesn't return to OS. The pattern aligns with kernel-selection path that chooses a large workspace for attention when kv_cache hits high.

lisa: Can you try forcing smaller workspace cap to see if it stabilizes? e.g. RW_WS_MAX=256MB or RW_ALLOW_WS_SHRINK=1

kevin: Tried RW_WS_MAX=256MB — reduced reserved baseline and growth stopped in short run. But we need to be careful: perf regressions for 512 prompts.

dmitri: Good experiment. Next step: confirm whether memory is genuinely reachable (i.e., allocator holds but not in use) or leaked (unreferenced GPU buffers). A quick check: run with --enable-gpu-alloc-trace and compare traces over time.

kevin: Started a trace and uploaded: s3://rwd-perf/repro/1812350001/alloc-trace-0.log

infra-bot: perf-snapshot-bot created snapshot: s3://rwd-perf/snapshots/1812350001/pynvml-2h.json

maria: Looking at alloc-trace: there are repeated dptr allocations from kvcache layer that never get freed until process restart. Stack shows path: runtime::kv_cache::insert -> workspace_acquire -> allocator::reserve.

aj: Hmm that suggests a retention in KV cache references rather than allocator leak. Maybe a subtle refcount bump on cache insert path when we hit batch merge case. Any recent change to kernel picker or batch heuristics?

kevin: We rolled a kernel-picker tweak two days ago to bias for fused attention kernel for seq >= 256. Patch: https://git.internal/r/redwood/infer/+/PR-4389.

lisa: Timeline fits. If fused kernel uses a different workspace layout and we forgot to account for reuse semantics, KV insert might be holding an extra reference.

dmitri: Quick local test: bisect kernel-picker commit range with canary image. If mem growth disappears on older commit, bingo.

kevin: Running a three-commit bisect now. Also adding a minimal C++ repro that allocates kvcache entries and frees them repeatedly to see if allocations are released:
```cpp
// repro/minimal_kv_leak.cc (run on GPU)
for (int i=0;i<100000;i++) {
  auto e = kvcache.insert(dummy_key, make_workspace(40MB));
  kvcache.erase(e);
}
```

maria: If erase doesn't free due to a lingering pointer in batch-merge list, that would explain it. Also check finalize/destruct ordering in fused-attn path.

aj: As mitigation for customers, we can: 1) pin kernel-picker to old behavior for Dedicated pools; 2) set RW_WS_MAX env to cap workspace; or 3) add periodic kvcache.compact() job (cheap). Which is easiest?

lisa: For now, set WS cap and schedule a canary rollback of kernel-picker if bisect shows regression. Also add kvcache compaction to background janitor.

kevin: Action items:
- kevin: finish bisect + post result (ETA 2h)
- dmitri: add alloc-trace diff tool to highlight never-freed allocations (ETA tomorrow)
- maria: prototype kvcache.compact() API and runbook (ETA EOD)
- aj: prepare rollback PR for kernel-picker and a guarded feature flag (ETA 3h)

dmitri: Quick observed clue — profiler fbprof shows that large workspace allocations happen right after a batching boundary when we merge small requests into a larger effective batch. Might be a batching-heuristic edge-case.

kevin: Bisect update: commit PR-4381..PR-4389 — culprit appears to be PR-4385 (kernel-picker bias for fused-attn). When I revert that patch, memory remains stable in 8h test.

maria: Great find. That implies fused-attn path introduced retention. Next: code review the PR for ownership semantics.

aj: I'll open rollback PR and also add a unit test that asserts kvcache size invariant after repeated inserts/erases under fused-attn.

lisa: Thanks everyone. If we have reproduction steps and s3 traces in one place I'll pin this thread and move to a short postmortem if needed.

kevin: Uploaded consolidated artifacts: s3://rwd-perf/repro/1812350001/{alloc-trace-0.log,pynvml-2h.json,debug-allocator.log,minimal_repro.cc}.

infra-bot: deploy-bot scheduled rollback to canary-kp=old on pool dedicated-az1 at 2026-03-18T16:30Z (initiated by aj)

maria: Closing loop — once rollback is live, run 24h verification and then prepare follow-up PR that fixes ownership in fused-attn instead of removing perf gains.

kevin: Verified 24h run on rollback image: no growth. Will prepare repro with small C++ harness showing leak in fused path.

lisa: Nice work. :party_parrot:
